content:
Data Gathering  
I downloaded 50-minute MP3 files  from a known source called Open to Debate . Using 
information -retrieval methods, I extracted the top 5 topics  that matched Elad’s project 
domain:  
• Childhood Obesity Guidelines: Good Medicine or Too Extreme?  
• Is Legalizing Marijuana a Mistake?  
• Debating the Legacy of the COVID -19 Pandemic  
• Psychedelics for Mental Health: Help or Hype?  
• Should We Legalize the Market for Human Organs?  
I prefer to focus on science-related topics rather than politics , since political debates 
tend to become heated and don’t always provide scientific explanations  
 
Speaker Diarization  
The next step was to classify which speaker spoke when . This process is called 
diarization  (from the word “diary” – יומן .)I used Pyannote.audio , the best open -source 
model I found, authenticated using a HuggingFace  token.  
Important notes:  
• The process is long and must be done offline . On CPU, a 50 -minute podcast took 
~20 minutes  to process.  
• The main challenge was not knowing how many speakers  appear in each debate.  
• The first speaker is labeled 𝑆0, and every new speaker is compared to all previous 
ones ( 𝑆0….𝑆𝑛−1). Complexity increases exponentially  as more speakers appear.  
• Debates include moderators + crowd questions , so total speakers are usually 5  - 8. 
In contrast, Elad’s simulator will likely include only one speaker , so no diarization will be 
needed.

JSON Output Structure  
After diarization, I created a JSON file storing each speaker’s speech segments.  
{ 
  "speaker" : "Jeremy Chapman" , 
  "start": 845.97, 
  "end": 857.0, 
  "duration" : 11.03, 
  "pauses" : [0.36, 0.48, 0.37, 0.22, 0.14], 
  "crowd_question" : false 
} 
 
I also added metadata  for each speaker to support future analysis:  
"speaker" : "Sally Satel" , 
"profession" : "Psychiatrist, Senior Fellow at the American Enterprise Institute" , 
"degree" : "M.D., Brown University" , 
"lecturer" : "Yale University School of Medicine" , 
"podcast" : "Should We Legalize the Market for Human Organs" , 
"total segments" : 21, 
"total duration" : 855.17, 
"crowd_questions_count" : 3, 
 
Now the data is ready for prosodic feature extraction.
